title: Exact anchors do not make every scale exact
question: How do fixed International System of Units (SI) anchors, measured gravity, and derived Planck scales belong in one scale map without becoming one kind of evidence?
answerPreview: The SI fixes selected defining values exactly, while G remains measured and Planck scales inherit its uncertainty; placing them on one normalized ruler compares magnitudes but predicts nothing new.
summary: Separate exact definitions, practical realizations, measured G, and Planck scales derived from hbar, c, and G, then use logarithmic normalization only as a labeled coordinate comparison.

observationStage.title: Definition and measurement status ledger
observationStage.question: Which displayed values are exact SI anchors, and which value comes from measurement?

items.label: Caesium-133 defining transition frequency
items.explanation: The SI fixes this numerical value exactly to define the second; a clock realizes the definition with stated practical uncertainty.

items.label: Speed of light in vacuum
items.explanation: The SI fixes this numerical value exactly and uses it with the second to define the metre; measured paths and realizations are not automatically exact.

items.label: Planck constant
items.explanation: The SI fixes h exactly as an action anchor used in defining the kilogram.

items.label: Newtonian constant of gravitation
items.explanation: This is the CODATA 2022 adjusted measured value of G, not an exact SI defining value; its standard uncertainty is 0.00015 x 10^-11 in the same unit.

items.label: Planck length
items.explanation: This CODATA Planck length is derived from hbar, c, and measured G. It is not a fixed SI definition or a direct observation of a minimum length.

observationStage.conclusion: Delta_nu_Cs, c, and h have exact defining numerical values in the SI. G is measured, so a scale derived using G is not promoted to exact status by also using exact constants.

guidedBlocks.title: Read the status before reading the digits
body: An exact defining value and a measured value can appear in the same equation without acquiring the same status.

The SI fixes the caesium transition frequency, the speed of light, and the Planck constant. Laboratories still realize the second, metre, and kilogram through physical procedures with practical uncertainty.
The gravitational constant G is measured. More displayed digits do not turn it into a fixed definition.

caveats: Exact definitions do not remove realization uncertainty.

guidedBlocks.title: A ruler organizes scales; it does not generate them
body: The activity places positive length, time, or mass values on a base-10 logarithmic ruler using their stated SI unit.

Defined, derived, measured, conventional, and illustrative entries remain visibly distinct even when two points lie close together. Exact IAU nominal values are conversion constants, not exact measured properties of an astronomical body.
Choosing one unit as the reference changes the numerical coordinate. It does not reveal a new law or predict an unlisted scale.

technicalBlocks.title: Planck scales are derived combinations
body: Using hbar = h/(2 pi), the conventional Planck length, time, and mass are l_P = sqrt(hbar G/c^3), t_P = sqrt(hbar G/c^5), and m_P = sqrt(hbar c/G).
Their dimensions follow from action, gravitation, and speed. Their numerical values depend on the chosen constants and unit coordinates.
Because h and c are exact in the SI while G is measured, these SI Planck-scale values inherit uncertainty from G.
technicalBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: Fixed h and c; CODATA G and Planck-unit relationships
caveats: Planck scales are conventional derived scales, not observations of a smallest length or time.

technicalBlocks.title: Normalization is a coordinate choice, not a prediction
body: For a positive quantity value Q expressed in its family SI unit U, the ruler coordinate is x = log10(Q/(1 U)).
The ratio inside the logarithm is dimensionless because Q and U have the same dimension and quantity kind.
Changing U shifts x by a constant. Setting a reference scale to numerical unity is normalization; it does not explain why nature realizes that scale.
technicalBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; PHYSICS_TOUR_MASTER_PLAN.md, 2026-07-26 contract
caveats: A logarithm of a dimensional numerical value is meaningful here only through the explicitly stated same-kind unit ratio.

equationSteps.label: Fixed SI anchors
equationSteps.explanation: These numerical values are fixed exactly by the SI; practical realizations remain physical procedures with uncertainty.
caveats: Exact SI values are not three uncertainty-free measurements.

equationSteps.label: Measured gravitational input
equationSteps.explanation: Parentheses state the CODATA standard uncertainty in the final displayed digits; G is measured rather than fixed by the SI.

equationSteps.expression: l_P = sqrt(hbar G/c^3), with hbar = h/(2 pi)
equationSteps.explanation: The combination has length dimension and inherits numerical uncertainty from measured G in SI coordinates.
